senses.gloss: ch.<cite ref="R00565">same</cite> <cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 2:5">Targ. Gen. II, 5</cite>.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Ezekiel 7:10">Targ. Ez. VII, 10</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Chullin 60b:6">Ḥull. 60ᵇ</cite> <he>שדי … ולא צ׳</he> he put seed in it, but it did not sprout, <he>אתא מיטרא וצ׳</he> a rain came, and it sprouted.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 2:3:3">Y. Kil. II, 27ᵈ</cite> <he>מן דזרע צַמְחִין</he> after he had sown, they (the vines which had been cut down) grew up again. Y. Maas. Sh. IV, end, 55ᶜ <he>צמחין</he> the wheat in the storehouse will sprout (and be ruined).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 132:17">Targ. Ps. CXXXII, 17</cite>; a. e.—

<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:1">Lam. R. to I, 1</cite> <cite ref="T00152"><he>רבתי</he></cite> (<he>חד כות׳</he> 1) <he>דאינון מַצְמְחִין עשבין וכ׳</he> that they (the wheat stores) shall produce sproutings, and this man (thou) shall have no benefit of them.
